writeup: TIC 348837498 is a candidate eclipsing binary star identified through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The system shows a primary eclipse with a depth of 6.03% and an orbital period of 4.3965 days, with no secondary eclipse detected. The eclipse signal achieved a detection significance of 157.0 in the Box Least Squares search, and pixel-level image analysis confirmed the signal with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 18.3, though the centroid offset of 7.7 arcseconds warrants further investigation. This candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a newly identified target. The machine learning screening assigned it a score of 0.39, indicating moderate confidence for a real eclipsing system.
